chunks: Fadhalah from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) said:
I asked him about meat, is it taken out of the Haram (sanctuary)? He said: 'Nothing is taken out of it except the snout (of the camel) after three days.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking meat out of the Haram sanctuary according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the prohibition of exporting meat from the Haram, a ruling rooted in the sanctity of the sanctuary and the practice of the Prophet. The specific exception of the camel's 'sanam' (often interpreted as the hump or a specific cut) after three days reflects the practical considerations of preservation and the distinct status of camels in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabian culture. It highlights the nuanced application of general prohibitions to specific, culturally significant items.
